en fil.explanation: "En fil" means "a file" on a computer. It is also a metal tool for smoothing things, like "en neglefil" (a nail file).

en filial.explanation: "En filial" means "a branch", as in a branch of a company. To say a company opens one in another town: "Vi åbner en filial i Odense" (We are opening a branch in Odense). Do not mix it up with "en afdeling" (a department): "Jeg arbejder i salgsafdelingen" (I work in the sales department).

en film.explanation: "En film" means "a film". To say more than one, add no ending: "Vi har set to film" (We have seen two films). To ask if someone has seen a film, use "set" (seen): "Har du set filmen?" (Have you seen the film?)

en filmaften.explanation: "En filmaften" means "a movie night". It is built from "film" (movie) and "aften" (evening). To suggest one, ask: "Skal vi have filmaften i aften?" (Shall we have movie night tonight?)

en filmstjerne.explanation: "En filmstjerne" means "a film star". It is built from "film" (movie) and "stjerne" (star). To talk about stars in the sky, use the same word "stjerne": "Der er mange stjerner i aften" (There are many stars tonight).

en filosof.explanation: "En filosof" means "a philosopher". To say what a person studies, use "filosofi" (philosophy): "Hun læser filosofi" (She studies philosophy).

en finale.explanation: "En finale" means "a final", as in the last match of a competition. To say a team gets that far, say: "De nåede finalen" (They reached the final). To talk about the big last part of a concert, use the same word: "Koncertens finale var flot" (The finale of the concert was beautiful).

en finanslov.explanation: "En finanslov" means "a national budget". It is built from "finans" (finance) and "lov" (law). In Denmark, the parliament "Folketinget" passes it each year.

en finger.explanation: "En finger" means "a finger". To say your finger hurts, Danish says "the finger" where English says "my finger": "Jeg har ondt i fingeren" (My finger hurts), literally "I have a pain in the finger".

en finne.explanation: "En finne" means "a fin". Another meaning is a person from Finland. To say someone is one, say: "Min ven er finne" (My friend is a Finn).

en firewall.explanation: "En firewall" means "a firewall". The word comes from English. To say you switch it off, use "at slå fra" (to switch off): "Slå firewallen fra" (Turn the firewall off).

en firkant.explanation: "En firkant" means "a four-sided shape". It is built from "fire" (four) and "kant" (edge). The part "kant" also appears in "en bordkant" (a table edge).

en fisk.explanation: "En fisk" means "a fish". In the plural, "fisk" has no ending: "tre fisk" (three fish). To say what you eat, use "at spise" (to eat): "Vi spiser fisk til middag" (We eat fish for dinner).

en fiskefrikadelle.explanation: "En fiskefrikadelle" means "a fish cake". It is built from "fisk" (fish) and "frikadelle" (a Danish meatball). A classic Danish dish is "fiskefrikadeller med remoulade" (fish cakes with remoulade, a cold sauce).

en fiskehandler.explanation: "En fiskehandler" means "a fishmonger". It is built from "fisk" (fish) and "handler" (a dealer). The word also means the shop itself. To say you go to the shop: "Jeg skal ned til fiskehandleren" (I am going down to the fish shop).

en fisker.explanation: "En fisker" means "a fisherman". To say what a fisherman does, use "at fange" (to catch): "Fiskeren fanger torsk" (The fisherman catches cod). Do not mix it up with "en fiskehandler" (a fishmonger): "Fiskehandleren sælger frisk laks" (The fishmonger sells fresh salmon).

en fiskerby.explanation: "En fiskerby" means "a fishing village". It is built from "fisker" (fisherman) and "by" (town). The part "by" also appears in "en storby" (a big city).

en fiskestang.explanation: "En fiskestang" means "a fishing rod". The last part "stang" (pole) also appears in "en flagstang" (a flagpole). In the plural, the vowel changes: "to fiskestænger" (two fishing rods).

en fjende.explanation: "En fjende" means "an enemy". To talk about an enemy that two sides share, say: "en fælles fjende" (a common enemy).

en fjer.explanation: "En fjer" means "a feather". In the plural, "fjer" has no ending: "tre fjer" (three feathers). To say a pillow is filled with feathers: "en pude med fjer" (a pillow with feathers).

en fjernbetjening.explanation: "En fjernbetjening" means "a remote control". It is built from "fjern" (far) and "betjening" (operation). "Betjening" also means "service", as in "god betjening" (good service).

en fjord.explanation: "En fjord" means "a fjord". In Denmark, "Limfjorden" is a fjord in northern Jutland.

en flagermus.explanation: "En flagermus" means "a bat", as in the animal. Literally, it is "flutter mouse", from "flagre" (to flutter) and "mus" (mouse). To say more than one, add no ending: "to flagermus" (two bats).

en flagstang.explanation: "En flagstang" means "a flagpole". The last part "stang" (pole) also appears in "en fiskestang" (a fishing rod). In the plural, the vowel changes: "to flagstænger" (two flagpoles).

en flamme.explanation: "En flamme" means "a flame". To talk about a former love, say: "en gammel flamme" (an old flame).

en flaske.explanation: "En flaske" means "a bottle". To say what is in it, put the drink right after it, with no word for "of": "en flaske vand" (a bottle of water).

en flaskeåbner.explanation: "En flaskeåbner" means "a bottle opener". It is built from "flaske" (bottle) and "åbner" (opener). The last part "åbner" also appears in "en dåseåbner" (a can opener).

en fletning.explanation: "En fletning" means "a braid". The matching verb is "at flette" (to braid): "Hun fletter sit hår" (She braids her hair).

en flirt.explanation: "En flirt" means "a flirt". The matching verb is "at flirte" (to flirt): "De flirter hele aftenen" (They flirt all evening).

en flise.explanation: "En flise" means "a tile". To say where it goes, put the place before it: "en gulvflise" (a floor tile) and "en vægflise" (a wall tile).

en flod.explanation: "En flod" means "a river". To name one, say: "Rhinen er en flod" (The Rhine is a river). Do not mix it up with "en å" (a stream), which is smaller: "Der er en å bag huset" (There is a stream behind the house).

en flok.explanation: "En flok" means "a flock". It also means "a crowd" of people. To talk about animals together, say: "en flok får" (a flock of sheep). To talk about people together, say: "en flok børn" (a bunch of children).

en flok fugle.explanation: "En flok fugle" means "a flock of birds". After "flok", the birds are plural: "fugle" (birds), from "en fugl" (a bird). The first part "flok" (flock) also works for other groups: "en flok får" (a flock of sheep) and "en flok børn" (a bunch of children).

en flue.explanation: "En flue" means "a fly". The word also appears in "en fluesmækker" (a fly swatter).

en flybillet.explanation: "En flybillet" means "a plane ticket". It is built from "fly" (plane) and "billet" (ticket). The part "billet" also appears in "en koncertbillet" (a concert ticket).

en flygtning.explanation: "En flygtning" means "a refugee". The word comes from the verb "at flygte" (to flee). To say people fled, use it in the past: "De flygtede fra krigen" (They fled from the war).

en flygtningestrøm.explanation: "En flygtningestrøm" means "a flow of refugees". It is built from "en flygtning" (a refugee) and "en strøm" (a stream). "Strøm" also means electric current: "Strømmen er gået" (The power has gone out).

en flyrejse.explanation: "En flyrejse" means "a flight". Do not mix it up with "et fly" (a plane): "Flyet er forsinket" (The plane is delayed). A "flyrejse" is the trip: "Flyrejsen var forsinket" (The flight was delayed).

en flytning.explanation: "En flytning" means "a move", as in moving to a new home. It comes from "at flytte" (to move). To say you are moving, use the verb: "Vi flytter i næste uge" (We are moving next week).

en flyttekasse.explanation: "En flyttekasse" means "a moving box". It is built from "at flytte" (to move) and "en kasse" (a box). "Kasse" also means "checkout" in a shop: "Betal ved kassen" (Pay at the checkout).

en flyverdragt.explanation: "En flyverdragt" means "a snowsuit". The word is "flyver" (a pilot) plus "dragt" (a suit). To talk about the suit a pilot wears, use the same word: "Piloten har en flyverdragt på" (The pilot is wearing a flight suit).

en flyvetid.explanation: "En flyvetid" means "a flight time". It is built from "at flyve" (to fly) and "en tid" (a time). "En tid" also means "an appointment", as in "en tid hos lægen" (an appointment with the doctor).

en flåde.explanation: "En flåde" means "a fleet". To talk about the vehicles of a company, say: "en flåde af lastbiler" (a fleet of trucks).

en flåt.explanation: "En flåt" means "a tick", as in the biting animal. In Denmark, ticks can spread an illness called "borreliose" (Lyme disease).

en flødebolle.explanation: "En flødebolle" means "a chocolate-covered marshmallow treat". It is a classic Danish sweet. The name is built from "fløde" (cream) and "bolle" (a bun).

en fløjte.explanation: "En fløjte" means "a flute". It also means "a whistle". To talk about a referee, say: "Dommeren blæser i fløjten" (The referee blows the whistle).

en fod.explanation: "En fod" means "a foot", as in the body part. To say your feet hurt, Danish says "the feet" where English says "my feet": "Jeg har ondt i fødderne" (My feet hurt), literally "I have pain in the feet". To say you go on foot, use "til fods": "Han kom til fods" (He came on foot).

en fodboldkamp.explanation: "En fodboldkamp" means "a soccer match". It is built from "fodbold" (soccer) and "kamp" (match). The part "kamp" also appears in other sports: "en tenniskamp" (a tennis match).

en fodboldspiller.explanation: "En fodboldspiller" means "a soccer player". It is built from "fodbold" (soccer) and "spiller" (player). The part "spiller" also appears in "en skakspiller" (a chess player).

en fodgænger.explanation: "En fodgænger" means "a pedestrian", literally a foot-goer, from "fod" (foot). The first part "fod" also appears in "en fodtur" (a walk on foot).

en fodgængerzone.explanation: "En fodgængerzone" means "a pedestrian zone". It is built from "en fodgænger" (a pedestrian) and "en zone" (a zone). In Copenhagen, "Strøget" is a famous street for pedestrians.

en fodnote.explanation: "En fodnote" means "a footnote". The name is built from "fod" (a foot) and "note" (a note), because it sits at the foot of the page. To point to one, write: "se fodnote 3" (see footnote 3).

en fodring.explanation: "En fodring" means "a feeding". It comes from "at fodre" (to feed an animal): "Jeg fodrer hestene" (I feed the horses).

en fold.explanation: "En fold" means "a fold". The matching verb is "at folde" (to fold): "Jeg folder papiret" (I fold the paper).

en folkeafstemning.explanation: "En folkeafstemning" means "a referendum". Do not mix it up with "et valg" (an election): "Der er valg i november" (There is an election in November). In 2000, Denmark held "en folkeafstemning om euroen" (a referendum on the euro).

en folkepension.explanation: "En folkepension" means "a state pension", literally a "people's pension". In Denmark, the amount depends on how many years you have lived in the country.

en folkeskole.explanation: "En folkeskole" means "a primary school". In Denmark, it is the public school for children from about age 6 to 16.

en forandring.explanation: "En forandring" means "a change". The matching verb is "at forandre" (to change): "Jeg vil forandre mit liv" (I want to change my life).

en forbandelse.explanation: "En forbandelse" means "a curse". To swear when something goes wrong, use the same word: "Forbandelse!" (Damn!)

en forbedring.explanation: "En forbedring" means "an improvement". It comes from "at forbedre" (to improve): "Vi vil forbedre servicen" (We want to improve the service).

en forbindelse.explanation: "En forbindelse" means "a connection". To say a phone or internet connection is bad: "Forbindelsen er dårlig" (The connection is bad). It also means a tie between two things: "Der er en forbindelse mellem søvn og humør" (There is a connection between sleep and mood).

en forbinding.explanation: "En forbinding" means "a dressing", as in a bandage for a wound. To ask for one, say: "Jeg har brug for en forbinding" (I need a dressing). Do not mix it up with "et plaster" (a Band-Aid): "Har du et plaster?" (Do you have a Band-Aid?)

en forbruger.explanation: "En forbruger" means "a consumer". It comes from "at forbruge" (to use up): "Vi forbruger meget strøm" (We use a lot of electricity).

en forbrydelse.explanation: "En forbrydelse" means "a crime". To say someone commits one, use "at begå" (to commit): "Han begik en forbrydelse" (He committed a crime).

en forbryder.explanation: "En forbryder" means "a criminal". It comes from "en forbrydelse" (a crime). To describe an act, use the adjective "kriminel" (criminal): "en kriminel handling" (a criminal act).

en fordel.explanation: "En fordel" means "an advantage". To weigh two sides, say: "fordele og ulemper" (advantages and disadvantages).

en fordeling.explanation: "En fordeling" means "a distribution". It comes from "at fordele" (to share out): "Vi fordeler arbejdet" (We share out the work).

en fordom.explanation: "En fordom" means "a prejudice". It is built from "for" (before) and "dom" (judgment). "Dom" also means a court verdict: "Dommen faldt i går" (The verdict came yesterday).

en forelæsning.explanation: "En forelæsning" means "a lecture". To say you are going to one, use: "Jeg skal til forelæsning" (I am going to a lecture).

en forening.explanation: "En forening" means "an association". To say you belong to one, say: "Jeg er medlem af en forening" (I am a member of an association).

en forespørgsel.explanation: "En forespørgsel" means "an inquiry". The matching verb is "at forespørge" (to inquire): "Jeg vil gerne forespørge om prisen" (I would like to inquire about the price). To talk about a search in a database, use the same noun: "en forespørgsel" (a query).

en forestilling.explanation: "En forestilling" means "a performance". To say you have no idea about something, use the same word: "Jeg har ingen forestilling om det" (I have no idea).

en forfader.explanation: "En forfader" means "an ancestor". It is built from "for" (before) and "fader" (father). In the plural, the vowel changes: "mine forfædre" (my ancestors).

en forfatter.explanation: "En forfatter" means "an author". To say who wrote a book, use "skrevet af" (written by): "Bogen er skrevet af en dansk forfatter" (The book is written by a Danish author).

en forfremmelse.explanation: "En forfremmelse" means "a promotion", as in a move to a higher job. The matching verb is "at forfremme" (to promote): "Chefen vil forfremme hende" (The boss wants to promote her).

en forgænger.explanation: "En forgænger" means "a predecessor". To talk about an earlier version of a thing, use the same word: "Bilen er forgængeren til den nye model" (The car is the predecessor of the new model).

en forhandler.explanation: "En forhandler" means "a dealer". To say what a dealer sells, put it before the word: "en bilforhandler" (a car dealer). Do not mix it up with "en forhandling" (a negotiation): "Forhandlingen tager lang tid" (The negotiation takes a long time).

en forhandling.explanation: "En forhandling" means "a negotiation". To say two sides are negotiating, use "i forhandlinger" (in negotiations): "De er i forhandlinger om en ny kontrakt" (They are in negotiations about a new contract).

en forhindring.explanation: "En forhindring" means "a hurdle", as in an obstacle. The matching verb is "at forhindre" (to prevent): "Regnen forhindrer os i at spille" (The rain prevents us from playing).

en forhøjelse.explanation: "En forhøjelse" means "an increase". To say what rises, put it before the word: "en skatteforhøjelse" (a tax increase).

en forklaring.explanation: "En forklaring" means "an explanation". The verb is "at forklare" (to explain): "Kan du forklare opgaven?" (Can you explain the assignment?)

en forkortelse.explanation: "En forkortelse" means "an abbreviation". Danish examples are "osv." for "og så videre" (and so on) and "FN" for "Forenede Nationer" (the United Nations).

en forkærlighed.explanation: "En forkærlighed" means "a fondness". The last part "kærlighed" means "love": "Kærlighed gør blind" (Love is blind).

en forkølelse.explanation: "En forkølelse" means "a cold", as in the illness. To say you have one, you can also use the adjective "forkølet": "Jeg er forkølet" (I have a cold).

en forlovelse.explanation: "En forlovelse" means "an engagement", as in a promise to marry. To talk about the person you are engaged to, say "min forlovede" (my fiancé or fiancée), the same word for both.

en forlovelsesring.explanation: "En forlovelsesring" means "an engagement ring". It is built from "forlovelse" (engagement) and "ring" (ring). To say someone proposed, use "at fri" (to propose): "Han friede til hende" (He proposed to her).

en forlover.explanation: "En forlover" means "a best man". The same word is used for a woman, as in "a maid of honor": "Hun er min forlover" (She is my maid of honor). Do not mix it up with "en forlovelse" (an engagement): "De fejrer deres forlovelse" (They are celebrating their engagement).

en forlygte.explanation: "En forlygte" means "a headlight". It is built from "for" (front) and "lygte" (lamp). The part "for" also means "front" in "et forsæde" (a front seat).

en forlystelsespark.explanation: "En forlystelsespark" means "an amusement park". It is built from "en forlystelse" (an amusement) and "en park" (a park). In Copenhagen, "Tivoli" is a famous amusement park.

en forlængelse.explanation: "En forlængelse" means "an extension", as in more time. To talk about a contract, say: "en forlængelse af kontrakten" (an extension of the contract). Do not mix it up with "en forlængerledning" (an extension cord): "Jeg har brug for en forlængerledning" (I need an extension cord).

en forlængerledning.explanation: "En forlængerledning" means "an extension cord". It is built from "forlænge" (to extend) and "ledning" (cord). "Forlænge" also works for time: "at forlænge en aftale" (to extend an agreement).

en form.explanation: "En form" means "a shape". To talk about a baking pan, use the same word: "Kagen bages i en form" (The cake is baked in a pan). To say someone is fit, use "i form" (in shape): "Han er i god form" (He is in good shape). Do not mix it up with "en blanket" (a paper form): "Udfyld blanketten" (Fill in the form).

en formand.explanation: "En formand" means "a chairman". It is built from "for" (in front) and "mand" (man). In the plural, the vowel changes: "to formænd" (two chairmen).

en formel.explanation: "En formel" means "a formula". To name what it works out, add "for": "formlen for arealet af en cirkel" (the formula for the area of a circle). The "e" disappears when you add an ending: "formlen" (the formula).

en formidler.explanation: "En formidler" means "a communicator". It also means "an intermediary". To talk about someone who passes things between two sides, say: "Han er formidler mellem kunden og firmaet" (He is the go-between for the customer and the company).

en formidling.explanation: "En formidling" means "a communication". It also means "mediation", as in helping two sides find each other. To talk about helping people find a home, use "boligformidling" (housing placement).

en formue.explanation: "En formue" means "a fortune". To say something costs a lot, say: "Det koster en formue" (It costs a fortune).

en formular.explanation: "En formular" means "a form". To tell someone to complete one, say: "Udfyld formularen" (Fill in the form). Do not mix it up with "en form" (a shape): "Cirklen har en rund form" (The circle has a round shape).
